note: mapping_basis=data_labels. DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2014_family.do infixes DA3032 at the ES3032 DATA LIST positions (P2801..P2807 = cols 236-242, identical to ES3032 line 22 and to the questionnaire's column codes (236)-(242)) under lower-cased names, and Bookmark 13 sets item = the variable name (p2801..p2807; lower-casing is Stata naming, a mechanical case change of the CIS code) -- nothing positional, so Step 5b is exempt and no verification_/verify_ files were written. LABELS vs QUESTIONNAIRE: ES3032 VARIABLE LABELS P2801, P2802, P2804, P2805, P2806, P2807 match the corresponding rows of the Pregunta 28 grid in cues3032.pdf character for character, 6/7 (read from a 300-dpi render of the scanned page 7, not OCR; the questionnaire's line breaks, e.g. 'entre / padres', 'los / abuelos', 'en la / pareja', rejoined; the '.' after 'intimidad' on the printed P2804 row runs into the dot leaders and is not in the label, so it is not shipped). P2803 DIFFERS IN GENDER-INCLUSIVE FORM ONLY: the label reads 'Las relaciones con los/as abuelos/as', the printed questionnaire 'Las relaciones con los abuelos'. Same statement, same column code (238), same order, so the code-to-text tie is unaffected. item_text ships the QUESTIONNAIRE wording for all 7 (what interviewers read aloud), matching batch_556's handling of the same pattern. VALUE LABELS identical on all 7: 1 'Aumenta' 2 'Disminuye' 3 '(NO LEER) Permanece igual' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.', matching the questionnaire's column headers (Aumenta, Disminuye, (NO LEER) Permanece igual, NS, NC). RESP BY DESIGN: the .do recodes 3 (the volunteered, not-read 'stays the same'), 8 and 9 to missing, so live resp is {1,2} and option rows ship for those two codes only. Dropped by the .do (p2801..p2807): code 3 427/955/1023/534/864/746/700, code 8 182/309/265/308/263/284/215, code 9 10/24/30/23/34/26/28. CHECKED ANYWAY, decisive: reading DA3032 (2464 records, all 385 bytes; id = row number) at cols 236-242, dropping 3/8/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex col 254 and cov_age cols 255-256 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 9998 rows both, 2096 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt rows, 0 resp and 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as the Stata value label (1 -> 'Hombre' 4886 rows, 2 -> 'Mujer' 5112, no cross cells). Live item x resp (1/2): p2801 359/1486, p2802 930/246, p2803 233/913, p2804 98/1501, p2805 285/1018, p2806 183/1225, p2807 193/1328 (per-item n 1845/1176/1146/1599/1303/1408/1521) -- every item uses both levels, and the one negatively-valenced item (p2802 family conflict) is the only one where Aumenta dominates, as the content predicts. Live values read from the local irw cache copy table_context.R had just written; validate_items.R --table-sets passed (7 items, resp {1,2}). No filter precedes P.28 (DA3032 holds no code 0 on any of the seven; the 368 absent ids answered 3/8/9 on all seven). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): instructions = the Pregunta 28 stem verbatim from cues3032.pdf, shared by all seven rows, so instructions not section_prompt, one trivial section; the stem carries no interviewer direction, so nothing was dropped. The stem frames every item as a consequence of family use of new technologies (Internet, mobile phone) -- the items are what that use increases or decreases, which the item_text rows alone do not say. The '(NO LEER) Permanece igual' option is not shipped because its code is absent from the live data. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3032 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by this project ('educación' in p2806 rendered 'upbringing', its usual sense in a parents-and-children context) -- issues-page line owed at upload. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, irw#2381, every CIS survey year) applied, not re-derived. Not an instrument-name mismatch: the dictionary description (parent-child communication, family conflict, relations with grandparents, privacy, couple communication, parental influence on education, doing things together, increasing or decreasing) matches the seven P.28 rows in order; it omits the new-technologies framing, which the shipped instructions carry.
public_note: Asks whether family use of new technologies (Internet, mobile phone) increases or decreases each aspect; respondents who volunteered 'stays the same' (code 3, not read aloud) are coded missing, so resp takes only 1 (increases) and 2 (decreases); item text English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
